newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude, heat vulnerable, trends hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude, heat vulnerable, trends hold.

text.p: NYMEX crude and heating oil futures were vulnerable to immediate weakness on Tuesday but some chartists said the uptrends were fully intact and it was too early to pick a top in the market.
"The trend is still clearly higher in the terms of the long term and even the short term," said Bob MacMinn, president of MPAS in Toronto.
He said crude's price action on Monday was negative, but it was forming a short-term triangle over the last four days that could be a continuation pattern.
Monday's trading was also an "inside trading day" that could imply a consolidation or pause to the rally, and not a new downtrend, he said.
"Picking tops in this market has not proved lucrative over the past four months," he said. "Nothing tells me to sell this market aggressively."
Jan crude has support at Monday's low of $24.98 and the Dec 6 low of $24.92, MacMinn said. He said strong resistance remains at $25.60-$26.10.
Heating oil is nearing critical support at 71.50 cents where an uptrend line off the lows from Nov 5 and Dec 2 crosses, he said, but prices still remain in a trading range between 70 and 75 cents.
But one Washington trader said heating oil had completed a five wave rally based on Elliott Wave analysis and dating back several months, which means any rally now should be sold.
He said heating oil may bounce initially on Tuesday to correct some of the losses over the last two days, before heading south to 70 cents.

"My feeling is a little negative," in crude oil, said Tony Machacek, a futures broker at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in London, citing a need for a retracement after recent strong gains. "It's probably got further room to the downside."

He put psychological support at $25 and then a further technical floor at $24.91, which was near the top of a previous downside key reversal. Further support was seen at $24.50, where its 13-day moving average crosses.
Resistance is at $25.25 and and $25.40, he said.
